summary: Nez Perce lookout first used in 1914 as a tent camp; the current L-4 cab on a 53-foot tower dates to 1953 and is used on an emergency basis.

access.note: Emergency-use lookout reached on foot by trail from the Elk City area. The sources do not describe public entry into the cab.

visit.trail_note: Hike-in. The Anderson Butte National Recreation Trail and other trails reach the summit; ask the Elk City Ranger Station about current conditions.

events.note: First lookout was a tent camp, per NHLR, firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts.
Climbing guide photo caption dates a log lookout cabin with cupola to 1932. NHLR gives only early 1930s for an L-4 cab on a short tower; the sources do not say whether these are one structure.
Current structure: L-4 cab on a 53-foot timber tower.
Jim Reid listed as known staff.
Mr. and Mrs. Kirkpatrick listed as known staff.
Shift to emergency-basis use. Sources say the 1980s (Idaho Fire Lookouts) or early 1980s (firelookout.com); 1980 marks the decade start only, not a dated event.

corrections.proposed: 1914 first lookout was a tent camp; current tower built 1953
corrections.why: NHLR says the first lookout was a tent camp in 1914 and the current structure was built in 1953. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists 1914 as Camp.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 6,827 ft (2,081 m); firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 6,847 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure (2080.9 m).

NHLR says an L-4 was placed on the summit in the early 1930s; the climbing guide's photo caption dates a log cabin with cupola to 1932. The sources do not say they are the same structure, so the story reports both.
NHLR calls the current structure a timber tower; firelookout.com calls it a 53-foot CT-2 tower with L-4 cab. These are compatible descriptions; the story uses the L-4 cab on a 53-foot tower.

notes_for_editor: Height 16.2 m is the 53-foot tower height from NHLR converted to metres (53 ft = 16.15 m); the sources give no other height. Staffing as_of is undated because the register and climbing guide pages carry no date. The 1932 caption and the early-1930s L-4 may be the same structure; unresolved. Access was 'unknown' in the record and is now restricted/hike-in based on the sources. Not read, but surfaced by search as a lead: a Nez Perce National Forest history PDF (fs.usda.gov/media/259214) that may list the 1953 towers; worth checking to confirm the 1953 date. No photos added: the climbing guide's photo credit has no image URL in the page read.
